topStories.headline: Council Picks Grass Fields for Lions Park, Approves Land for New Animal Shelter
topStories.dek: The Waxahachie City Council voted this week to move forward on two long-discussed city projects: a natural-grass playing-field renovation at Lions Park and the purchase of a 20-acre site for a new animal shelter.
topStories.body:
After years of discussion and multiple competing proposals, the Waxahachie City Council voted at its September 22 meeting to advance the redevelopment of Lions Park using natural grass practice fields rather than synthetic turf. The Waxahachie Community Development Corporation had earlier pledged $5.8 million toward the project at its July 8 meeting, and the council's vote this week locks in the grass-field option as the preferred design.

At the same meeting, the council approved the purchase of a 20-acre parcel on US 287 Business to serve as the site for a new animal services building — a step the Waxahachie Daily Light described as moving the long-sought shelter 'one step closer to reality.' The current shelter operates out of 191 Lions Park Road, a location that would be freed up as part of the broader Lions Park redevelopment.

Residents from the Waxahachie Skatepark Initiative had urged the council during public comment to include a skate park in the Lions Park plan, arguing the city sits in a regional gap for skate facilities. The council did not add a skate park to the current plan, though advocates indicated they will continue to press the case.

Both decisions came in a single session, underscoring the council's push to close out projects that have been in planning for several years as the city's population continues to climb toward an estimated 50,000 residents.

topStories.headline: Waxahachie–Midlothian Regional Trail Comment Period Closes Today
topStories.dek: The public comment period for a proposed 2.3-mile shared-use trail connecting FM 875 to Getzendaner Park ends September 25, 2026.
topStories.body:
TxDOT and the City of Waxahachie have been gathering public input on a proposed 12-foot-wide concrete trail running approximately 2.3 miles between FM 875 and Getzendaner Park. The project is part of the larger Midlothian-to-Waxahachie Regional Trail corridor, which would eventually link the two cities via an approximately 9.8-mile shared-use path.

The city hosted a virtual public meeting and an in-person open house on September 10 at the Waxahachie Civic Center. Plans also call for reconstructing the frontage road beneath I-35E to accommodate a roughly 10-foot-wide trail alongside a single travel lane separated by a safety barrier.

All written comments must be received by September 25, 2026 — today — to be included in the project record. Comments may be submitted by mail to Kimley-Horn and Associates, 13455 Noel Road, Two Galleria Office Tower, Suite 700, Dallas, TX 75240, or by email to kelly.saladis@kimley-horn.com. Project materials and responses to comments will be posted at waxahachietx.gov under the 'Latest News' section.

Construction of the Waxahachie segment of the regional trail had been projected to run from early 2026 into early 2027, though that schedule is subject to the completion of environmental clearance, right-of-way acquisition, and utility relocation work.

topStories.headline: Texas Roadhouse Heading to Waxahachie After Council Approves Economic Development Deal
topStories.dek: The Waxahachie City Council approved a Chapter 380 economic development agreement in August, clearing the way for Texas Roadhouse to build at I-35 and U.S. Highway 287.
topStories.body:
The Waxahachie City Council approved a Chapter 380 economic development agreement with Roadhouse Enterprises Inc. at its August 18 meeting, paving the way for Texas Roadhouse to construct a restaurant in the city. Public filings show the planned location at the intersection of I-35 and U.S. Highway 287 in Waxahachie, with permitting records indicating a construction completion target of June 2027.

Texas Roadhouse, known for hand-cut steaks, fall-off-the-bone ribs, and its signature honey cinnamon butter rolls, has nearly 800 U.S. locations. The Waxahachie agreement marks the chain's entry into Ellis County, where residents have previously had to drive to neighboring communities to access the brand.

The announcement comes as Waxahachie continues to attract new commercial investment amid rapid population growth. Separately, a 75-acre mixed-use development called Palmetto Road — with a $35 million first phase comprising 15 multifamily buildings and 915 total planned garden-style units — filed a construction start date of September 15, 2026, with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

moreNews.headline: City Puts FY 2026-27 Budget and Tax Rate in Place After 3-2 Council Vote
moreNews.body: The Waxahachie City Council approved its budget and tax rate for fiscal year 2026-27 at its September 8 meeting by a 3-2 vote, according to the Waxahachie Daily Light. The Ellis County Commissioners Court had separately approved its own budget for FY 2026-27 in late August and was expected to adopt a tax rate shortly thereafter; Commissioners had voted 4-1 to set the proposed rate at 27.3992 cents per $100 valuation.

moreNews.headline: Ellis County Burn Ban Remains in Effect
moreNews.body: Ellis County has been under a county-wide burn ban since the Commissioners Court voted to impose one at its July 21, 2026 meeting. As of the Ellis County website's most recent update, the ban remains in effect for all unincorporated areas of the county. Residents with questions can visit elliscountytx.gov/573/Burn-Ban.

moreNews.headline: Fire Station #1 Rebuild Moves Toward October Construction Start
moreNews.body: The City of Waxahachie is working with construction manager Key Construction Texas LLC to replace Fire Station #1 at 1475 Spur 394. The project calls for a new 12,178-square-foot single-story building with four apparatus bays, sleeping quarters, kitchen, offices, training space, and a storm shelter. Subcontractor bids were due September 10, and construction is scheduled to begin October 2026, according to the city's news flash page.

moreNews.headline: WISD Discusses Future Uses for Former Coleman Building and Admin Offices
moreNews.body: Waxahachie ISD trustees discussed competing proposals for the district's former Coleman building at a recent board session, as reported by the Waxahachie Daily Light on September 21. The building currently houses Challenge Academy, the district's school of choice program, special education, and centralized registration. Proposals under consideration include moving the pre-kindergarten program from Turner Elementary into the Coleman building's northern wing, or relocating the Little Chiefs Academy childcare program to address crowding at the district's administrative offices.
